hooks.text: Half your body's atoms came from distant galaxies.
Are half the atoms in your body from another galaxy?
50 percent of your body originated outside our galaxy.

title: Half of You Came From Another Galaxy
description: Up to half of the matter in the Milky Way originated from distant galaxies. Intergalactic winds carried those atoms across space to form our Solar System.

beats.text: Half your body's atoms came from distant galaxies.
beats.visual: Hubble deep field visual showing distant spiral galaxies, 2004

beats.text: Up to 50 percent of the Milky Way originated outside our galaxy.
beats.visual: Illustration of intergalactic transfer of matter between galaxies

beats.text: Edwin Hubble proved other galaxies existed back in the 1920s.
beats.visual: Edwin Hubble sitting at the 100-inch Hooker Telescope, 1923

beats.text: Our Solar System takes over 200 million years to orbit the galaxy.
beats.visual: Diagram of Solar System orbiting inside the Orion Arm of Milky Way
queries: Solar System orbit Milky Way diagram

beats.text: At the center sits Sagittarius A*, a supermassive black hole.
beats.visual: Event Horizon Telescope image of Sagittarius A* black hole, 2022
queries: Sagittarius A star Event Horizon Telescope

beats.text: NASA's Chandra observatory caught it unleashing a flare 400 times brighter than normal.
beats.visual: Chandra X-ray Observatory image of X-ray flare from Sagittarius A*

beats.text: Powerful intergalactic winds blew massive amounts of matter between galaxies.
beats.visual: Supercomputer simulation of intergalactic winds transferring gas between galaxies

beats.text: That dust built our planet, our Sun, and us.
beats.visual: Artist rendering of early protoplanetary disk forming Earth and Sun

beats.text: That is why half your body's atoms came from distant galaxies.
beats.visual: Composite photo of starry night sky and Milky Way galaxy
